 Sasha Jovanovic Sun, October 25, 2026 at 3:07 AM MST 4 min read XIOR.BR +2.52% 
 Xior Student Housing stock closed at €24.40 on Friday, roughly flat over the past week but still down sharply over the last three months. Fresh Q3 2026 results now put that price in a harsher light. Reported net income of €38.57 million and a trailing net margin above 50% look strong at first glance, yet part of that profitability reflects a €51.1 million one off gain that flatters the recent track record. 
 For anyone thinking beyond today, the bigger story is the tension between that inflated earnings base and the ongoing strain from debt coverage over the coming years. 
 Like the high reported margin at Xior Student Housing but uneasy about earnings boosted by a one off gain and ongoing debt coverage pressure? Check out our screener of list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals stocks (205 results) for companies where profits rely less on accounting quirks and more on recurring strength. 
 Q3 2026 Earnings Summary 
 Revenue (Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025): €54.493 million vs. €50.55 million (up about 7.8%) 
 Net Income excl. extra items (Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025): €38.567 million vs. €3.512 million (very large year on year increase, helped by a strong uplift in underlying profitability before the separate one off gain) 
 Basic EPS (Q3 2026 vs. Q3 2025): €0.659 vs. €0.075 (very large year on year increase per share) 
 Net Margin excl. extra items (TTM to Q3 2026 vs. TTM to Q3 2025): 50.5% vs. 38.3% (higher profitability on a trailing twelve month basis, before the separate one off gain) 
 Earnings tell one story, but investors who care about valuation often give more weight to the cash flowing through the business. Looking at Xior Student Housing's cash flows alone, the stock could be a dramatic 45% undervalued . 
 ENXTBR:XIOR Trailing 12-Month Earnings & Revenue History as at Oct 2026 Xior bullish story leans on earnings quality test 
 For anyone leaning optimistic on Xior Student Housing, the Q3 2026 print offers mixed but useful support. Revenue sits higher than a year ago and the trailing net margin excluding extra items is above 50%, which lines up with a resilient student housing model that converts rent into profit efficiently. EPRA earnings rising 6% over nine months, helped by 4.62% like for like rent growth and 98.5% occupancy, suggests that day to day operations are doing the heavy lifting rather than just that €51.1 million gain. 
 Debt worries and one offs keep the bear case alive 
 Bears still have plenty to point to. Headline net income is flattered by the €51.1 million one off, so the recent surge in EPS and net margin can overstate ongoing earning power. Concerns around leverage also remain relevant, even with €137 million of available credit lines improving liquidity. A share price that has fallen about 12% over three months indicates that investors are not treating the latest numbers as a clean bill of health for Xior Student Housing yet. 
 Story Continues After a quarter where Xior Student Housing leans on a one off gain and stretched debt cover, it is worth asking whether these headlines capture the full risk picture or if they obscure deeper balance sheet and earnings quality issues that only come into focus once you review our risk analysis for Xior Student Housing which shows 2 important warning signs . 
 Hunt For Mispriced Earnings Power 
 Xior Student Housing shows how headline profit and balance sheet pressure can diverge when investors focus on near-term reported numbers. The real opportunity is finding stocks where recurring earnings power and valuation still appear out of sync.
